note_text: Reciprocating engines use pistons that move back and forth in a linear motion, not in circles. This back-and-forth movement is converted into rotation by a crankshaft. Engines that spin internally to generate power are known as rotary or turbine engines. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocating_engine https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/reciprocating-engine
claim: Reciprocating engines are engines that spin in circles, similar to a diesel engine.
context: There are also medium-speed reciprocating engines: engines that spin in circles, like a diesel engine.

source_verification.reasoning: Both cited sources directly support the note's claims: pistons move linearly (back and forth), this is converted to rotation by a crankshaft, and engines that spin internally are rotary/turbine engines. The Wikipedia article explicitly mentions rotary engines as those that set cylinders in motion around the shaft. All factual claims are covered.

citations.quote: A **reciprocating engine**, more often known as a **piston engine**, is a [heat engine](/wiki/Heat_engine "Heat engine") that uses one or more [reciprocating](/wiki/Reciprocating_motion "Reciprocating motion") [pistons](/wiki/Piston "Piston") to convert high temperature and high [pressure](/wiki/Pressure "Pressure") into a [rotating motion](/wiki/Circular_motion "Circular motion").
citations.explanation: Supports that reciprocating engines use pistons (linear motion) converted to rotation, not engines that spin internally.

citations.quote: In most types, the linear movement of the piston is converted to a rotating movement via a [connecting rod](/wiki/Connecting_rod "Connecting rod") and a [crankshaft](/wiki/Crankshaft "Crankshaft")
citations.explanation: Directly supports the note's claim that linear piston motion is converted to rotation by a crankshaft.

citations.quote: Some designs have set the cylinders in motion around the shaft, such as the [rotary engine](/wiki/Rotary_engine "Rotary engine").
citations.explanation: Supports the note's distinction that engines which spin internally are rotary engines.

citations.quote: A [reciprocating](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/reciprocate "Definition of reciprocating") engine is an engine in which a piston is moved up and down in a cylinder by a [mechanism](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mechanism "Definition of mechanism") such as a crankshaft and [connecting](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/connect "Definition of connecting") [rod](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/rod "Definition of rod").
citations.explanation: Supports that the piston moves back and forth and is connected via crankshaft.

citations.quote: A reciprocating engine has pistons moving back and forth inside.
citations.explanation: Directly supports the note's claim about back-and-forth piston motion.

citations.quote: An alternative to the reciprocating engine is the rotary piston engine.
citations.explanation: Supports distinction between reciprocating and rotary engines.
